title: [rereview] project-LICHEN-dk3c.5: TOCTOU race in set_dodag_state — loss timer scheduled outside mutex
description:
In lichen_announce_sched_set_dodag_state (announce.c:744-752), the dodag_loss_work timer scheduling (line 748) and cancellation (line 751) both execute after the mutex has been released (at line 735 or 741). Between the unlock and the k_work_schedule/k_work_cancel_delayable call, the dodag_loss_resume_handler work handler could fire, observe the stale dodag_joined state, and call schedule_next() with a potentially wrong interval. Specifically:

1. set_dodag_state(false, ...) schedules dodag_loss_work at line 748.
2. Before the work fires, set_dodag_state(true, ...) is called. It unlocks at line 741 (else branch since prev_gateway == new_gateway when transitioning from gateway to... wait, no. Actually the scenario is simpler:

- set_dodag_state(true, false) releases the mutex at line 735 or 741.
- Between that release and the k_work_cancel_delayable at line 751, the dodag_loss_resume_handler (scheduled by a prior set_dodag_state(false, ...)) fires and calls schedule_next().
- The handler reads dodag_joined=true (just set by the concurrent set_dodag_state), schedules with the gateway interval.
- Then the cancel at line 751 runs, but the work has already been rescheduled.

Fix: move the timer scheduling/cancellation inside the mutex scope. Or better, restructure so that the dodag_loss_resume_handler just sets a flag and the interval selection in schedule_next() checks both dodag_joined and the loss flag atomically.

File: lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/announce.c:744-752
